title: Passageway Anchors: Guided Flows & Signposting for Console Navigation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers and internal users report confusion when moving between high-level org views (workspaces, teams) and task-specific surfaces (routes, model dashboards, rollout pages). The existing sidebar and workspace switcher are dense and don't surface destination semantics: diagnostic dashboards, rollout controls, and per-route cost views feel buried.

Goal: Design a navigation model that reduces time-to-context and mistakes when switching workspaces or surfacing cost/rollout dashboards. The proposal introduces the "Passageway Anchors" pattern: contextual entry corridors in the left rail that reveal signposted destinations (Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost Lenses, Deployments) and an adaptive workspace switcher that preserves breadcrumbs, active filters, and quick actions.

Scope: Primary focus on information architecture and micro-interactions for the left rail, workspace switcher, and per-route contextual surface. Includes clickable prototypes, annotated flows for rollouts and cost views, and handoff artifacts for engineering and PMs.
comments: 2026-02-22 Maya Chen: Initial whiteboard session with PM and Eng (Rafael Ortega). We mapped 12 task flows where users drop context after switching workspaces; prioritized rollouts and cost dashboards as highest friction.
2026-02-28 Design critique: multiple reviewers prefer the 'entry corridor' metaphor over nested menus; concerns about vertical real estate on narrow screens noted (see tradeoffs below).
2026-03-03 Usability plan approved: 6 moderated sessions (mix of infra PMs and product engineers), plus an analytics A/B prototype to validate time-to-task and mis-click rate.

2026-03-09 Engineering sync: agreed on a phased implementation. Phase 1 = visual-only left rail + workspace switcher modal; Phase 2 = contextual signposting tied to route-level telemetry and cost lenses. ENG dependency list created (ENG-8421, ENG-8542).
2026-03-12 Ava Thompson: Updated prototype after review; pushed new flows to figma and linked PRD. Requesting final UX sign-off and FE/Eng sizing for phase 1 components.
design_decisions: Use a two-tier left rail: stable global anchors (Home, Models, Billing) + contextual passageway groupings that expand on hover or keyboard focus.
Workspace switcher becomes a focused modal preserving 'active filters' and a 'resume context' action that restores open route tabs when moving back to a workspace.
Expose a compact cost lens badge on route rows that opens an inline cost panel rather than a full page for quick scoping.
Rollouts surface will be promoted to a first-class signpost in the passageway for teams with >50% rollout activity (runtime heuristics defined in analytics doc).
acceptance_criteria: Interactive prototype validated in Figma with annotated flows for: workspace switch, open rollout, open cost lens, and resume context.
FE implementation plan with component list, accessibility checklist (keyboard nav, aria), and responsive behavior for widths down to 1024px submitted to ENG.
Analytics instrumentation checklist completed and QA-ready, including events for 'switch_start', 'switch_resume', 'cost_lens_open', 'rollout_open'.
Moderated usability tests completed with qualitative notes and at least 4/6 participants showing reduced confusion compared to baseline.
Design handoff package (tokens, micro-interaction specs, edge cases) uploaded to the repo and linked in PRD.
success_metrics: Reduce average time-to-target (workspace -> rollout page) from current baseline by 30%.
Decrease nav-related support tickets from workspace confusion by 40% in first 60 days post-launch.
Increase usage of inline cost lens by 25% among active dev teams during beta.
Keyboard navigation success rate 100% for core flows in QA pass.
risks: Vertical space: expanded passageways could push primary content below the fold on smaller viewports — mitigate with collapse affordances and compact mode.
Overload: exposing too many destinations in the rail may confuse new users. Mitigation: progressive disclosure and telemetry-driven signpost promotion.
Engineering complexity: restoring 'resume context' requires stateful session storage across workspace boundaries; dependent on ENG features (see dependencies).
Analytics noise: early telemetry may be noisy until instrumentation and sampling are tuned.
next_steps: Finalize Figma micro-interactions and export component kit (due 2026-03-16).
Engineering sizing session for Phase 1 (week of 2026-03-15).
Lock analytics event schema and send to ENG for instrumentation work.
